text: A man sits in the shade of a striped awning, indigo wound about his head, watching the heat move.
"You came up out of the south on foot," he says, "in that." He looks at what you are wearing.

choices.text: What is wrong with what I am wearing?

text: Ibn Abn has not moved. The shade has.

choices.text: What is wrong with what I am wearing?

text: "Ibn Abn. I cross this, and then I cross it again."
"There is no third thing I do."

choices.text: What is wrong with what I am wearing?

text: "Water in the middle, and everything alive within a day's walk of it."
"Jackals work the open ground between here and there. They are not brave. They only have to be quicker than you are tired."

choices.text: What is wrong with what I am wearing?

text: "They eat above your head and see further than you ever will. Nothing hunts them. Nothing needs to."

choices.text: What is wrong with what I am wearing?

text: "It is cut for a cold country. Out there it will take the water out of you and give it to the sun."
He unfolds a bundle from beside him: heavy linen, an indigo mantle, a sash.
"I carry two. A man who carries one is a man who has never torn one."

choices.text: I have nothing to trade for it.

text: "Then you owe me, and an owed thing crosses the sand better than a paid one."
He puts the bundle in your hands and goes back to watching the heat.
"As you like. It will be here, and so will I."
"Wear it before the middle of the day, not after."
He has already stopped looking at you.
"You are still walking," Ibn Abn says. "So it fits."
